name: Megan Holloway

five_sec.what_is_it: Meal kit boxes, with a pick-a-box prize pop-up
five_sec.who_for: Couples and small families who want ingredients shipped
five_sec.trust_why: Big real brand, but the box game is pure gimmick
five_sec.next_step: Continue Without Offer and look at plans

full_page.what_stopped_me: A meal kit for nine people? Half the menu is Parmesan, cheddar and crema, so it's no good for my dairy-free girl, and the price hides behind a zip code

HF.quote: A box to open for a prize! Cute, but for nine of us 'Cheesy Smashed Burgers' is a second mortgage, and half the menu is dairy!

five_sec.who_for: Planners like me with a big recipe collection
five_sec.trust_why: Four years of using it, and the 4.8 rating matches my experience
five_sec.next_step: Check whether the Black Friday sale is on
five_sec.delivers_food_why: It's the recipe-and-list app I know

full_page.what_stopped_me: Nothing! The 'Nov 27-30, $24.50/year' sale means I'm renewing. My only wish: the 'Deliver Groceries' button still doesn't name Walmart, so I'm retyping my list
full_page.whats_missing: A real one-tap Walmart cart; auto-scaling for 9 that I don't have to fuss with

PTE.quote: Nov 27-30, $24.50 a year! I'm stocking up. Still wish 'Deliver Groceries' said Walmart by name.

five_sec.who_for: Families who want to be told what to cook
five_sec.next_step: Check if I can bring my own recipes
five_sec.delivers_food_why: 'How It Works' shows a phone and a list

full_page.what_stopped_me: Fixed menus: fifteen plans of their recipes, and 'Can I use the eMeals app to shop and cook other recipes?' is a collapsed FAQ with no answer showing. I had to dig for the price too
full_page.whats_missing: Importing my 300 recipes; family size; visible price

EM.quote: Fifteen plans of somebody else's recipes. I have 300 of my own! And I had to dig for 'How much does eMeals cost?'

five_sec.who_for: Parents who want dinner decided for them
five_sec.next_step: Scroll to see if it uses my recipes

full_page.what_stopped_me: The AI writes 'a recipe just for you'. I want MY recipes. And $25 a month is half a year of Plan to Eat in one month
full_page.whats_missing: Recipe import; big-family proof; reasonable price

OL.quote: 'Writes a recipe just for you': sweet, but my sourdough-mom heart wants MY recipes. And $25 a month is half my year of Plan to Eat!

five_sec.what_is_it: Plans the week, the family votes by text, then one tap fills an Instacart or Walmart cart
five_sec.trust_why: Clear and honest ('We don't deliver food'), but no big family anywhere
five_sec.next_step: See a sample week and look for a family size limit
five_sec.delivers_food_why: It says 'We don't deliver food' in bold

full_page.what_stopped_me: The free one-tap Walmart cart is exactly the reel I saw! Dairy-free is listed, a per-person profile could cover my 9-year-old, and $39/yr beats $49. But there's no way to bring my 300 recipes, the sample is 'Family of 4' with no size limit stated, and it's five weeknight dinners when I plan two weeks at a time
full_page.whats_missing: Recipe import; 'up to 9+' family size; planning more than one week

DD.quote: The free Walmart cart is what I came for! But where do my 300 recipes go, and does 'family size' go to nine? The sample is four.

dd_offer.why: It's spelled out in the pricing box and FAQ: no card, 14 days, then the free plan
dd_offer.expect_day_15: Back to the free plan, I keep the Walmart cart, no charge since there's no card.

head_to_head.reason: My 300 recipes live there and the $24.50 sale makes it a no-brainer

EM.reason: A free Walmart cart beats paying for someone else's fixed menu

PTE.reason: My own recipes and two-week planning; DinnerDrop can't import them

OL.reason: Free and honest versus $25 a month of AI recipes

HF.reason: Nine people and a dairy-free kid rule out boxes

dd_fix_that_would_move_me: Home page 'What you get': say plainly whether I can add or import my own recipes, and state the family size it plans for (show a family of 9 example).
